study: Sector lead-lag: when a sector ETF makes a sector-specific move up, do its members that have not moved yet (laggards) catch up over the next 10 minutes by more than the spread?
registered_at: 2026-10-14 premarket (~06:00 ET), before any bar for this study was fetched or any return computed.
origin: docs/PLAN_2026-10-14.md stage 1, idea 3 (operator 10/14: 'test it'). A causal discovery rule: it seats a name before its own move, from a move it can see in its sector.
prior: Weak. tools/studies/sector_study.py (9/14-9/23, book names, 8 days) found sector strength did not predict runway (memory runway-is-findable-profit-is-not-yet); that tested sector strength as a gate on names already seated, not lead-lag across a universe. Intraday sector lead-lag in liquid US names is widely arbitraged.

universe.names: HOLDINGS in tools/studies/sector_laglead_study.py: about 15 large holdings per sector ETF (173 names), each name in exactly one sector (semiconductors in SMH, Alphabet/Meta in XLC, Amazon/Tesla in XLY), frozen 2026-10-14 from knowledge dated before the test window. No board membership, so no selection on the scored days' moves (skeptic round 1 #2, #4). The sector of a name is the ETF list it is in; no industry mapping.
universe.per_day_filters: 20-session mean dollar volume >= $20M (SIP daily, split-invariant) and the day's raw SIP 09:30 open >= $10 (not the split-adjusted prior close, #8). A name with no SIP bars on any of the 26 days is removed from the universe and listed.
universe.frozen_digest: holdings_digest() is printed with every result.

signal.feed: Detected on IEX 1-minute bars (what the live desk can see): the last IEX close at or before a minute, looking back at most 15 minutes. Outcomes on SIP.
signal.sector_move: At minute m (09:50-15:20 ET): ETF IEX close(m) / close(m-5) - 1 >= +0.25%, AND that minus SPY's same 5-minute return >= +0.10% (a sector move, not the market).
signal.laggard: A universe member mapped to that ETF whose own IEX close(m) / close(m-5) - 1 <= +0.05% and >= -0.50% (has not moved, and is not falling apart).
signal.fire: Each laggard at each qualifying m, 30-minute refractory per symbol. An EPISODE is a run of consecutive qualifying minutes of one ETF; fires within it are not independent.

outcome: Gross 10-minute markout: SIP close of minute m+10 / SIP open of minute m+1 - 1 (early_entry_honest.markout).
cost: 10 bp round trip for the graded net; the pass also needs net > 0 at 20 bp.
statistic: Day-equal mean of per-day means, day-clustered t. Control (graded, #1): for each fire, a random minute of the same name and day within 60 minutes either side of the fire (inside 09:50-15:20) where the name is in the laggard band but its sector condition is FALSE, more than 30 minutes from any of that name's fires, held the same way (seeded sha of symbol|day|minute|laglead-v2). Lift = fire gross - control gross.
split: Half A = 2026-09-08..09-24, half B = 09-25..10-13 (the same calendar split as the early-entry and board-name studies).
pass: PASS only if in BOTH halves: net at 10 bp > 0 with t >= 2.0; net at 20 bp > 0; lift vs the no-sector-move control > 0 with t >= 2.0; net at 10 bp > 0 with entry at the SIP open of m+2 (latency, #3); net at 10 bp > 0 after dropping the 3 best days, and after dropping the ETF with the most fires (#5); >= 100 fires, >= 20 distinct ETF episodes, >= 10 sessions, and a control found for >= 80% of fires (coverage is printed per half). Short of fires, episodes or sessions = UNDERPOWERED; any FAIL half = FAIL. Interpretation fixed now (#10): a PASS whose lift vs the sector ETF's own next 10 minutes is <= 0 is sector momentum, not lead-lag, and the design would trade the ETF, not its members.
information_only: lift vs a later same-name minute (entry+1..+60)
lift vs a same-sector LEADER (up >= +0.50% over the same 5 minutes) at the same minute
lift vs the sector ETF's next 10 minutes (see the interpretation under pass)
fires on a fresh IEX bar at the signal minute vs a carried close (#9)
drops: removed names, ADV unknown/low, under $10 open, missing bars
data_integrity: Fetches run after 16:15 ET only (stop launching at 03:30), back off on 429, and never cache a day with a failed chunk. Scoring ABORTS (no verdict) if any of the 26 days lacks bars, any day lacks SPY or any ETF's bars, or more than 5% of universe name-days lack bars or ADV (#7).
no_retuning: +0.25% / +0.10% / +0.05% / -0.50% thresholds, 5-minute window, 30-minute refractory, 10-minute hold, the universe rule and the cost are fixed.
if_pass: Provisional: repeat on >= 10 forward sessions, then a result-skeptic review of the positive, then a live seating design (sector ETFs on the real-time stream).
if_fail: Sector lead-lag is closed as a discovery rule on free data.
script: tools/studies/sector_laglead_study.py: --fetch (daily bars, IEX + SIP minute bars for the frozen holdings, the ETFs and SPY; mini, after 16:15), default inventory with no returns, --score after a result-skeptic READY.
amended: 2026-10-14 premarket, before any bar was fetched, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST: frozen ETF-holdings universe replaces board names (no industry mapping, no Finnhub); graded same-name no-sector-move control; m+2 latency bar; episodes >= 20, drop-top-3-days and drop-largest-ETF bars; every information line implemented; aborts on missing SPY/ETF/days; $10 floor on the raw 09:30 open; fresh vs carried line; beta interpretation fixed. Round 2 (final): control window widened to +-60 min with >30 min exclusion (the same-hour window could not cover the open and :29-:30 fires); coverage >= 80% per half or UNDERPOWERED; text fixes (173 names, script field).
